page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a dedicated Cloud GPU server powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz without hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 180.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.25 GB of RAM per core. For accelerated workloads, it includes a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, offering 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data highlights the server's capabilities in machine learning and data processing. In LLM inference tests using a medium 7B model, the server achieved top-tier performance with 6293.73 tokens per second for prompt processing and 153.1 tokens per second for text generation. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also reached top-tier levels at 15.59 GB/sec, while multi-threaded decompression registered at 238.14 GB/sec. General CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core (34834.61) and Passmark CPU score (40930.36), fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show 173.77 GB/sec for large-block reads and 66.7 GB/sec for large-block writes.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high density of GPU memory and system RAM relative to its 16-core CPU allocation, making it a resource-dense option for specialized workloads. However, a notable hardware tradeoff is the lack of hyperthreading and a relatively low base CPU clock speed of 2.0 GHz, which positions its general-purpose compute performance in the average tier. This server is highly suited for workloads such as large language model inference, AI model deployment, data decompression pipelines, and memory-intensive GPU-accelerated computing.
